title: Time and Space Complexity Intuition
learningObjectives: Explain the topic and its assumptions.
Describe why it matters in solving programming problems.
Interpret a small example or trace.
Apply the idea to a new situation.

understand.concept: Efficiency describes how work and extra memory grow as input size increases. Time complexity models operation counts, while space complexity estimates additional storage. These growth models are not exact stopwatch readings.
understand.whyItMatters: Efficiency reasoning helps estimate scale and distinguish algorithmic work from hardware or timing noise.
understand.analogy: A sequential scan grows with the number of entries; a prepared lookup structure may use storage but speed repeated queries.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies the concept; real behavior depends on input, constraints, and implementation details.

explain.narrative: Define the task and assumptions, choose a method, trace it on a small example, then check edge cases. Efficiency describes how work and extra memory grow as input size increases. Time complexity models operation counts, while space complexity estimates additional storage. These growth models are not exact stopwatch readings.

examples.title: One pass
examples.explanation: A single pass over n items grows proportionally to n.

examples.title: Nested passes
examples.code: let c=0; for(let i=0;i<3;i++)for(let j=0;j<3;j++)c++; console.log(c);
examples.explanation: Two nested n-length loops produce n squared checks.

examples.title: Accumulator storage
examples.code: let total=0; for(const v of [1,2,3])total+=v; console.log(total);
examples.explanation: One accumulator is fixed extra storage.

examples.title: Output growth
examples.code: const out=[]; for(const v of [1,2,3])out.push(v*2); console.log(out.length);
examples.explanation: Output storage grows with input size.

examples.title: Count iterations
examples.code: let steps=0; for(const v of [4,5,6,7])steps++; console.log(steps);
examples.explanation: Iteration counting is a simple work estimate.

commonMistakes: Using a method without checking assumptions.
Confusing theoretical growth with exact runtime.
Failing to explain limitations or trade-offs.
